s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, itchy skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques on the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Symptoms have been present for more than 10 years
Lesions are localized to the left shin
Lesions are itchy
Milia are present in the superficial dermis
Erosions with partially detached epidermis are present
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination reveals dermoepidermal separation
Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1

shortlist.label: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: COL7A1 gene mutation and dermoepidermal separation

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
shortlist.why_kept: Family history and clinical presentation of itchy skin lesions with milia

shortlist.label: Kindler Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia

shortlist.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and histopathologic findings

raw.rationale: The presence of dermoepidermal separation, milia, and erosions with partially detached epidermis, along with the identification of a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1, are characteristic of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.

rejected.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
rejected.why: Lack of family history and specific genetic mutations typical of EBS

rejected.label: Kindler Syndrome
rejected.why: Absence of extracutaneous involvement and specific histopathological features

rejected.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: Lack of mucous membrane involvement and specific genetic mutations

rejected.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita
rejected.why: The disease onset is congenital and the presence of a genetic variant in COL7A1, which is not typical of EBA
